reason: The one-entry helper proposals are the clearest feasible group: the supplied helper already computes each 32-row band, and the feasibility review gives the panel pointer and scratch resets. They test transition overhead, but the prior sixteen-call wrapper showed mixed paired results and does not establish that transitions caused them. Treat these three IDs as overlapping descriptions of one experiment, not separate tests. Scratch reuse and packed-B traversal have explicit mappings but require larger assembly changes; their benefits are unmeasured. Transpose fusion is still more complex. The three two-K loop proposals overlap, and the supplied current full512 loops process one K step per iteration, so their required two-K body is absent. Transpose-aware full-shape work also requires a new generated helper that is not supplied. No proposal has evidence of a cache bottleneck or a gain above target.
